The successful completion of the Perinatal Education Programme (PEP) is expected to lead to improved obstetric practice. According to the retrieved matches, completion of the PEP's obstetric manual has already resulted in an improvement in midwives' knowledge about obstetrics but did not detect any alteration in their clinical practices. This suggests that while education and training are crucial for improving obstetric care, practical application of this knowledge is also necessary.

In other words, completing the PEP's obstetric manual is essential for acquiring knowledge, but actual practice changes require hands-on experience and supervision. Therefore, successful completion of the programme contributes to improved obstetric practices by enhancing midwives' understanding and skills, but it does not alone guarantee these improvements in clinical settings without further implementation and support.
